name: חיבור שני שברים עם מכנה משותף (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

questiontext:
Express the following, as a single fraction:

\[ {{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}}. \]

Leave your answer in its lowest terms in the form \(\frac{a}{b}\).

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The denominators are equal, so add the numerators and keep the denominator; then cancel any common factor.
Step 1 — The denominators are equal
In this case the denominators of the fractions are equal so you simply add the numerators to obtain the numerator and the denominator stays the same.

The general rule is:

\[ \frac{a}{b} + \frac{c}{b} = \frac{a+c}{b} \]

In this example:

\[ {{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}} = \frac{{{CT:2}}+{{CT:3}}}{{CT:4}} = {{CT:5}}. \]

Step 2 — Lowest terms
The greatest common divisor of the numerator and the denominator is \(\gcd({{CT:6}},{{CT:7}})={{CT:8}}\).[[if test="{{CT:12}}"]] Cancel this common factor:

\[ \frac{{{CT:9}}}{{{CT:7}}}=\frac{{{CT:10}}\cdot {{CT:8}}}{{{CT:11}}\cdot {{CT:8}}}={{CT:5}} \]

Now the numerator and the denominator have no common factor other than 1, so the answer is in lowest terms:[[else]] So nothing cancels: the fraction is already in lowest terms:[[/if]]

\[ {{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}}={{CT:5}} \]

on_true.feedback: Remember that the first step in adding fractions is to make both denominators equal. It is not simply adding the numerators and the denominators.
Simplify the fraction fully into the form \(\frac{a}{b}\) and leave in its lowest terms.
